subject: Premium support & regional surcharge — packaging and retainer options
messages:
From: Michael Chen <michael.chen@brightcart.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Premium support ask + geo surcharge question

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the product overview today — BrightCart is close to selecting a vendor for inference serving and we have two procurement questions before we move to contracting: 1) do you have a published regional surcharge for multi-region coverage (we need US + EU) and 2) can you outline retainer/response-band pricing for 99.9% vs 99.95% uptime (we care about on-call escalation windows and a named escalation engineer for sev1).

We attached our RFP excerpt (Brightcart_RFP_v3.pdf). High level: expected steady-state token volume looks like ~4B monthly, pilot in Q1 with a 6–8 week ramp. We are evaluating a Dedicated commit vs Reserved + burst model. If a multi-region commit reduces the surcharge, we'd consider an 18‑month commit.

Can you share a ballpark pricing matrix and any packaging suggestions that would reduce unit cost while preserving rapid response guarantees? Also curious about any onboarding retainer or runbook work — will that be billed separately?

Appreciate it —
Michael
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightCart

Attachments: Brightcart_RFP_v3.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Michael Chen <michael.chen@brightcart.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Premium support ask + geo surcharge question

Hi Michael — thanks for the RFP and the convo yesterday. Short answers up front: we do apply a geography surcharge for cross-region Dedicated pools, but it can be materially reduced with an expanded commit or if you accept asymmetric response windows in non-primary regions. Onboarding runbook+SOW work is typically a one-time SOW line item; we can fold a scaled onboarding credit into multi‑year deals.

I'll send a concise matrix (below) for pricing bands and then loop in Solutions and Finance to confirm margins. Preliminary approach attached: Redwood_SLA_matrix_v1.pdf.

High-level proposal (ballpark):
- 12‑month commit, Dedicated, 99.9% uptime: base retainer $12K/month + per-token pricing X — standard escalation (8hr business hours primary, 24/7 paging for sev2+ with on-call rotation)
- 18‑month commit, Dedicated, 99.95% uptime: base retainer $20K/month + lower per-token X-20% — includes named escalation lead and 2 on-call credits per month; geo surcharge reduced by 60%
- Pilot (3 months): reduced commit, onboarding retainer $8K (one-time), transition credit if upgraded to 18 months within 60 days

Next steps: Jonas and Laura, can you validate the staffing commitments and whether the geo-surcharge reduction is operationally safe for EU workloads? Vivek — can we do a preliminary discount authority on the 18‑month path to get an anchor for Michael?

Thanks —
Stephanie
Director, GTM Pricing
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_matrix_v1.pdf (pdf, 80KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Premium support ask + geo surcharge question

+1 on Stephanie's summary. A few operational clarifications to feed back to BrightCart: 

- Geo surcharge rationale: additional provisioned reserved capacity per region (replication, standby pools, and cross-region KV sync) — if BrightCart commits to steady-state throughput thresholds per region, we can reduce the surcharge because we avoid fragmented standby capacity.
- Escalation coverage: for 99.95% we propose a named escalation lead (x1) plus a 24/7 on-call roster for sev1. Onboarding runbook includes a 2-week runbook workshop + 1 embedded ops week (SOW line).
- Suggested retainer banding (operational minutes):
  * Bronze: 99.9% — 8hr primary response, business hours RTO, no named lead
  * Silver: 99.95% — 4hr response primary, 24/7 paging, named escalation lead, 2 on-call credits / mo
  * Gold: 99.98% — 1hr response, 24/7 priority channel, on-call rotation with guaranteed swap SLA (higher retainer)

If BrightCart needs EU compliance that affects data residency, runbook scope increases (audit evidence + additional on-prem connectors) — call that an onboarding delta that we'll price separately.

I'll draft a short MA plan with thresholds that would trigger the reduced geo surcharge (e.g., >60% traffic in EU for 12 months).

-Jonas
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Michael Chen <michael.chen@brightcart.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Premium support ask + geo surcharge question

Michael — quick note from Solutions on the runbook and escalation mechanics so you have the operational picture:

- Runbook deliverables: runbooks for deployment, incident playbooks per sev level, contact roster, and a 1-week onsite (or virtual) run-through. Typical SOW line: 40–60 hours (SOW_draft.docx).
- Named escalation lead: acts as first escalation for sev1 during agreed coverage window; lead does not replace on-call but expedites vendor-side remediation and liaises with your SREs.
- SLA crediting: we use time-weighted credits on rolling 30-day windows; design decision is to keep failover policies flexible (auto‑fallback to regional variant).

Operational ask: Michael, to reduce the geo surcharge we need a confirmed expected EU QPS distribution for the pilot (even rough %) and whether EU data must stay in EU. If data residency is required, that increases onboarding and may limit our ability to reduce surcharge.

Happy to run a short joint workshop next week — I can bring the runbook template.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW_draft.docx (docx, 45KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2026 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Premium support ask + geo surcharge question

Finance view — we can offer up to 15% standard discount off list on the 18‑month commit if BrightCart prepays at least 6 months; an additional 5% is doable for 100% prepay at contract signature and an agreed minimum monthly throughput. Any service credit exposure must be limited to standard SLA credit caps (we should not accept unlimited liability).

I'll sign off on the reduced geo surcharge proposal subject to: (a) minimum regional throughput thresholds in the MA plan, (b) EU data residency requirements documented, and (c) an onboarding SOW that scopes audit evidence. If Legal wants to tighten SLA credit caps, route to me for commercial exceptions.

-Vivek
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Chen <michael.chen@brightcart.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@brightcart.com
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Premium support ask + geo surcharge question

Thanks everyone — that was helpful. A few quick replies and next steps: 

- BrightCart is happy to target the 18‑month commit if Redwood will waive the geo surcharge for the EU region for the first 9 months of the contract (we'll accept the reduced surcharge thereafter). This helps us justify the multi-region pilot budget to our CFO.
- EU data residency: yes, EU user PII must remain in EU but inference results can be mirrored offshore. We can provide expected % traffic for EU in the next 48 hours.
- Pricing: please send a formal commercial summary/term sheet and a DocuSign link; we'll need a redline on the SLA focusing on credit caps.

We'll sign the DocuSign if the geo waiver for the first 9 months is in the term sheet and Vivek confirms the discount path. Please send the term sheet and I'll route to procurement.

Best —
Michael Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightCart
